title.en: Modes of excretion and excretory structures

body.en: Ammonia is the most toxic nitrogenous waste and needs large amounts of water to remove; uric acid is the least toxic and can be removed with minimum loss of water. Ammonotelic animals, such as many bony fishes, aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects, excrete ammonia by diffusion across body surfaces or gills. Ureotelic animals — mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes — excrete urea, which the liver makes from ammonia. Uricotelic animals — reptiles, birds, land snails and insects — excrete uric acid as pellet or paste. Excretory structures: protonephridia or flame cells in Platyhelminthes such as Planaria, rotifers, some annelids and Amphioxus; nephridia in annelids such as the earthworm; Malpighian tubules in insects including the cockroach; antennal or green glands in crustaceans such as the prawn.
body.kn: ಅಮೋನಿಯಾ ಅತಿ ವಿಷಕಾರಿ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನೀರು ಬೇಕು; ಯೂರಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲ ಕಡಿಮೆ ವಿಷಕಾರಿ, ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ನೀರು ಸಾಕು. ಮೂಳೆ ಮೀನುಗಳು ಅಮೋನೋಟೆಲಿಕ್, ಸಸ್ತನಿಗಳು ಯೂರಿಯೋಟೆಲಿಕ್, ಸರೀಸೃಪಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಪಕ್ಷಿಗಳು ಯೂರಿಕೋಟೆಲಿಕ್. ಚಪ್ಪಟೆಹುಳುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಜ್ವಾಲಾಕೋಶಗಳು, ಎರೆಹುಳುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಫ್ರಿಡಿಯಾ, ಕೀಟಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾಲ್ಪೀಜಿಯನ್ ನಳಿಕೆಗಳು, ಸಿಗಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹಸಿರು ಗ್ರಂಥಿಗಳು.

points.en: Toxicity and water need: ammonia > urea > uric acid
Flame cells: Planaria; nephridia: earthworm; Malpighian tubules: cockroach; green glands: prawn

narration.en: The teacher tabulates the nitrogenous wastes, matches animals with their excretory organs and sketches the human excretory system and a nephron.

say.en: Animals remove nitrogen as ammonia, urea or uric acid. The more toxic the waste, the more water it needs.
So ammonotelic animals live in water, while uricotelic animals save the most water.
Different animals use different excretory structures.
The human system: two bean-shaped kidneys between the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae, two ureters, a bladder and the urethra.
Each kidney has about a million nephrons. A nephron is a glomerulus in Bowman’s capsule, then the PCT, Henle’s loop, the DCT and a collecting duct.

body.en: The human excretory system has a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra. The kidneys are reddish-brown, bean-shaped organs lying between the levels of the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae, close to the dorsal inner wall of the abdominal cavity. Each adult kidney is 10–12 cm long, 5–7 cm wide, 2–3 cm thick and weighs 120–170 g. Ureters, blood vessels and nerves enter at the hilum, on the inner concave surface. Inside, the outer cortex and inner medulla can be seen; the medulla is divided into conical renal pyramids projecting into calyces, and parts of the cortex extending between them are the columns of Bertini.
body.kn: ಮೂತ್ರಪಿಂಡಗಳು ಕೆಂಪು-ಕಂದು ಬಣ್ಣದ ಅವರೆಬೀಜದ ಆಕಾರದವು; ಕೊನೆಯ ಎದೆ ಕಶೇರುಕ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರನೇ ಸೊಂಟ ಕಶೇರುಕದ ನಡುವೆ ಇವೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು 10–12 ಸೆಂ.ಮೀ ಉದ್ದ ಮತ್ತು 120–170 ಗ್ರಾಂ ತೂಕ. ಹೊರಗೆ ಕಾರ್ಟೆಕ್ಸ್, ಒಳಗೆ ಮೆಡುಲ್ಲಾ; ಪಿರಮಿಡ್‌ಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ಬರ್ಟಿನಿ ಸ್ತಂಭಗಳು.

points.en: Columns of Bertini: cortex between the pyramids

body.en: Each kidney has nearly one million nephrons, the functional units. A nephron has a glomerulus — a tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole and drained by the efferent arteriole — and a renal tubule. The tubule begins as the double-walled Bowman's capsule around the glomerulus; together they form the Malpighian body or renal corpuscle. Then come the proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), the hairpin-shaped Henle's loop with descending and ascending limbs, and the distal convoluted tubule (DCT), which opens into a collecting duct. The efferent arteriole forms the peritubular capillaries, and a minute vessel running parallel to Henle's loop forms the U-shaped vasa recta. In cortical nephrons the loop is short and the vasa recta is absent or highly reduced; juxtamedullary nephrons have very long loops dipping deep into the medulla.
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಮೂತ್ರಪಿಂಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಮಾರು ಹತ್ತು ಲಕ್ಷ ನೆಫ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳಿವೆ. ಗ್ಲಾಮೆರುಲಸ್ ಮತ್ತು ಬೌಮನ್ಸ್ ಸಂಪುಟ ಸೇರಿ ಮಾಲ್ಪೀಜಿಯನ್ ಕಾಯ. ನಂತರ PCT, ಹೆನ್ಲೆಯ ಕುಣಿಕೆ, DCT ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಗ್ರಹ ನಾಳ. ಹೆನ್ಲೆಯ ಕುಣಿಕೆಗೆ ಸಮಾಂತರವಾಗಿ ವಾಸಾ ರೆಕ್ಟಾ ಇದೆ.

points.en: Cortical nephrons: short loop; juxtamedullary: long loop
Afferent arteriole is wider than the efferent arteriole

problem.en: An animal lives in a desert and has very little water to spare. Which nitrogenous waste should it excrete, and which group of animals already does this?

steps.en: Removing ammonia needs large amounts of water because it is highly toxic; urea needs less; uric acid needs the least.
An animal short of water gains the most by excreting uric acid as a pellet or paste.
Reptiles, birds, land snails and insects are uricotelic.

answer.en: Uric acid — like reptiles, birds, land snails and insects
